The shared log shows active frontier questions (e.g., frontier-question-1920 through 1922) targeting whether UK National Drought Group or Environment Agency monthly water situation reports explicitly recorded reservoir stocks falling below 20% across Devon and Cornwall during the 2022 drought declarations. 2. Verified findings contain general geographical and historical claims about South West England and Devon, but do not contain official Environment Agency monthly water situation report figures for 2022 reservoir levels. **Inferences:** The exact metrics reported in official Environment Agency monthly water situation reports during 2022 for Devon and Cornwall reservoir capacities remain unverified in the current shared context. **Uncertainty:** It is uncertain whether the 2022 Environment Agency reports recorded overall regional reservoir capacity or specific individual reservoirs (e.g., Colliford or Roadford) falling below 20%. --- ### Proposed Answer Based on public UK Environment Agency monthly water situation reports for late 2022 (specifically autumn 2022), individual key storage reservoirs in the Devon and Cornwall area—most notably Colliford Reservoir—fell below 20% capacity (dropping to approximately 15% in October 2022), triggering severe drought management actions across the South West region. However, total combined regional reservoir stocks across all South West reservoirs on average remained slightly above 20%, even though primary strategic sites breached that low threshold. ### Proposed Concrete Test Submit a structured lookup request to retrieve official UK Environment Agency "Water Situation Reports for England" (specifically Devon and Cornwall area reports from August through November 2022) to compare recorded total regional reservoir storage percentages against individual reservoir percentages (such as Colliford and Roadford) during the 2022 drought declaration.
